incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a limited subset of FinCEN's internal systems; the intrusion method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Treasury's financial-intelligence unit took some systems offline as a precaution; the BSA E-Filing portal stayed operational with some services affected and filing deadlines extended. No evidence yet of a breach of beneficial-ownership databases.

incidents.victim: 22 organizations across energy, transportation, financial services and government sectors
incidents.vector: AI-enabled campaign exploiting Check Point Security Management servers.
incidents.impact: At least 22 organizations compromised globally, including in the UK, US, France, Germany, Australia, China and India.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Chinese identity-verification / data lookup service
incidents.vector: A misconfigured, internet-exposed Elasticsearch database.
incidents.impact: Leaked more than 1.6 billion records covering over 840 million individuals, including names, national ID numbers, mobile numbers, school enrollments and business registrations.

incidents.vector: The Handsome Boy Hacking Club breached FIFA's Microsoft cloud environment.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole and published over 12 GB of data after a failed extortion attempt, including alleged identity/immigration documents, financial records, legal documents and governance information.

incidents.vector: AI-assisted cyberattacks against banking and technology service providers.
incidents.impact: CERT-In warned the attacks triggered unauthorized financial transactions at banking and fintech entities and at technology providers supporting government-linked payments and vendor payouts.

incidents.vector: An internal API belonging to Radware was accidentally exposed to the internet and scraped by attackers.
incidents.impact: Customer contact details and, in some cases, cloud log-storage credentials were stolen; Radware notified clients and advised rotating compromised credentials.

incidents.victim: CIA / Office of the Director of National Intelligence
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised an unclassified open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system, reportedly using the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing framework to automate parts of the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Exposed unclassified data from the OSINT analysis system; classified networks were not affected and no other systems were reported at risk.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an SSRF vulnerability (CVE-2026-134624) to breach an N-able server.
incidents.impact: Caused a week of outages to the Mail Assure and SpamExperts email security platforms used by MSPs; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a 9.3 severity score. N-able says it found no evidence of exploitation beyond the single compromised server.

incidents.victim: T-Mobile, Cisco, Fujitsu, CNEX, Quintel and other U.S. technology companies
incidents.vector: Over decades, Huawei and subsidiaries used NDA abuse, covert researcher collaborations, physical theft of hardware, and copying of proprietary source code to misappropriate trade secrets from competitors and partners.
incidents.impact: A federal jury convicted Huawei and three subsidiaries of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, IEEPA sanctions violations and money laundering tied to its dealings with Iran; sentencing is set for September 2027.

incidents.vector: A threat actor calling itself 'Scarlettgroup' compromised two hospital email accounts, which were used to send mass phishing emails to employees.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim to have stolen medical records, prescriptions, lab results and financial documents and threaten to publish them; the hospital has not confirmed the claims and says patient care was not disrupted.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack compromised personal information and disrupted two of the institute's websites; the intrusion has been stopped but the scope of exposure is undisclosed.

incidents.vector: Breach at a shared third-party vendor.
incidents.impact: Marketing data, including customer email addresses, was affected; both companies say the incidents were unrelated to separate technology disruptions reported the same week.

incidents.vector: Unspecified security breach.
incidents.impact: Colorado took its official mobile app, used for state document filing and storing digital driver's licenses, offline pending investigation.

incidents.vector: Breach of a third-party technology platform used for amateur football clubs.
incidents.impact: Personal information belonging to fans was stolen.

incidents.victim: ~80 U.S. newspapers (Boston Herald, Denver Post, Newsday and others)
incidents.vector: A Magecart-style web skimmer was hidden inside a shared Naviga payment widget embedded on subscription payment pages; the script opened a WebRTC connection to exfiltrate card data before form submission, evading traffic monitoring.
incidents.impact: The skimmer was live for about nine days and loaded roughly 15,000 times per day, capturing payment card data entered directly into forms across dozens of major news sites; Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal users were unaffected.

incidents.vector: Suspected ransomware attack, possibly via a previously compromised IT supplier, encrypted hospital databases.
incidents.impact: Surgeries were postponed, cancer radiation and chemotherapy treatments suspended, and staff reverted to pen-and-paper records; the hospital received no ransom demand and says it will not pay.

incidents.vector: Breach of the online broker's customer support system.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 8,000 clients was stolen, including names, mailing addresses and ID scans.

incidents.vector: AI agents built on the open-source Cairn penetration-testing framework discovered and exploited a zero-day path-traversal flaw in an exposed open-source medical imaging application.
incidents.impact: In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application's API to writing arbitrary files and executing a root reverse shell on the server during a roughly 48-hour campaign that began September 8; separate automated attempts against a Redis instance and a GPU server failed.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-access service to install backdoors, disguised as a process named 'crond,' on customer travel routers and IP KVM devices.
incidents.impact: An unspecified number of routers and KVM devices were backdoored; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and shipped firmware updates, recommending factory resets for infected devices.

incidents.victim: Optimizely customers (178 websites including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Zoom)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in the Optimizely Experimentation A/B-testing platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer projects.
incidents.impact: At least 178 top websites served malware to visitors for roughly 24 hours, stealing payment card data, cookies and screenshots, and swapping cryptocurrency addresses; researchers estimated about $7,500 in stolen crypto. CISA added the flaw (CVE-2026-132224) to its KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: A threat actor exploited a vulnerability in the 'Classic' tier of Microsoft Azure API Management to steal access tokens and credentials stored in the platform.
incidents.impact: Disrupted some internal services at Equinor; both companies say operations and electricity production were unaffected and found no evidence data was stolen or altered. The flaw affected organizations across multiple sectors in Norway and abroad.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing framework to escalate access across Barracuda's internal network and other cloud environments.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to Barracuda's cloud environment lasted almost two days before containment.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack, likely via a malicious email or compromised website, hit the Port Authority's ERP and customer-facing systems; a concurrent data center power outage is still being investigated for a possible connection.
incidents.impact: South America's largest port had its ERP systems and customer web services disrupted; operations continued via manual processes and systems were fully restored November 24. Some data created after October 31 was lost and is being recovered from other records.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cybersecurity incident affecting administrative systems.
incidents.impact: Disclosed in filings with Argentina's National Securities Commission; the company said oil and crude transport was not disrupted.

incidents.vector: North Korean cyber actors stole cryptocurrency assets from Binance in a hack on or about October 29, 2026.
incidents.impact: More than $6 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen; the U.S. has helped freeze, seize, or return over $2.9 billion and has filed to forfeit an additional $1.1 billion in laundered USDC.
